title: PULP tech_cells_generic
_note: PULP's technology-cell wrappers: the behavioural stand-ins every PULP design
instantiates for clock gating, clock muxing, SRAM and power management, plus
the deprecated `pulp_clock_*` / `cluster_clock_*` / pad / memory cells that
older IP still uses.  These are the LIBRARY CELLS the other PULP families
(axi, common_cells, register_interface, cheshire, snitch, pulpissimo) carry
as closure-only roots, so this family measures them directly for once.
src/fpga is excluded, and the reason is recorded in core-v-mcu.json too:
tc_clk_xilinx.sv and tc_sram_xilinx.sv define THE SAME module names as
src/rtl/tc_clk.sv and src/rtl/tc_sram.sv (tc_clk_gating, tc_clk_mux2,
tc_sram, ...), so compiling both is a duplicate definition, and the Xilinx
flavour instantiates `BUFGMUX`, a vendor primitive the repository never
defines.  src/deprecated is KEPT -- unlike the copy core-v-mcu vendors, this
checkout's deprecated directory holds no *_xilinx.sv files, and its module
names do not intersect src/rtl's (checked, not assumed).
tc_sram_blackbox is excluded: it is a BLACK BOX declaration with no logic, so
synth yields an empty module and the miter reports `Can't find gold module
\\gold` (core-v-mcu.json records the same shape for a 105-port module with
no body).  Measuring it proves nothing either way.
First local sweep 2026-10-29: 53 rows, 49 / 50 elaborate, **44 / 50 proven**,
46 co-sim PASS and **53 / 53 with 0 undriven** -- every row in the family,
including the ones that are not comparable.  What is left is all accounted
for and none of it is a reader lead:
* THREE SAT-budget rows -- tc_sram, tc_sram_impl and generic_memory go over
the memory cap, which is what a 1024 x 128 memory array does to a miter.
* TWO rows have no read_slang reference because they are SIM-ONLY timing
cells: tc_clk_delay and pulp_clock_delay are `assign #(Delay) out_o =
in_i;`, and read_slang refuses `'tc_clk_delay' is not a valid top-level
module`.  generic_rom is the third, for its memory initialisation.
* pad_functional_pd and pad_functional_pu report `differs`, and it is a
MITER SOUNDNESS limit rather than a reader defect: both are bidirectional
pads driving `inout wire PAD` to 1'bz with pull-high / pull-low
resistors, and a miter over tri-state needs `tribuf -formal` to mean
anything (caliptra-ss's spi_host_axi_synth is recorded the same way).
Neither co-simulates, so there is no second opinion either; they are not
counted as leads.
